About: Topple or Slide — Which Gives Way First

Source

Concept
Under a horizontal push, the normal force does not sit at the centre — it migrates toward the leading edge. Toppling is the moment it reaches the edge and cannot move further.
Serves
Rotational equilibrium, torque balance, competition between toppling and sliding thresholds.
Inquiry
Push high on a tall block → topples. Slide the push down to the base — does it still topple, or slide?
Misconception
"Normal force acts at the centre of the block." — In fact it acts wherever it must to balance the torques.

Guided Inquiry

1 · Watch a high push

The block is tall and narrow. The push is applied high up (near the top) and grows slowly with time. Press ▶ Play and watch the green N arrow at the base — where does it sit, and where does it go as the push builds?

Notice: N is not at the centre. It slides forward.

2 · Predict — drop the push to the floor

Now imagine you slide the push height right down to near the base of the same tall, narrow block. Same block, same friction, same growing push — only the height changes. What happens?

3 · Watch a low push

The push height is now near the floor. Press ▶ Play again and watch the two thresholds on the right — Ftopple has climbed, Fslide has not. Whichever is smaller triggers first.

4 · The one thing to notice

Play with all three sliders. In every case, watch the green N arrow at the base:

As you push harder, N slides toward the leading edge — and toppling is simply the moment it runs out of block.

N does not sit at the centre. It sits wherever the torques demand.

Thresholds

▾
Ftopple—
Fslide—
Outcome—
Whichever threshold is smaller triggers first. Fixed: m = 5 kg, block height h = 1.0 m, g = 9.81 m/s².
Torque balance about the front-bottom corner (imminent toppling)
At the moment of toppling the normal force N sits exactly at the front-bottom edge, its lever arm about that pivot is zero, and no further shift is possible.
Sliding threshold (static friction limit)
Independent of the push height a. Lower the push and Ftopple rises past Fslide, so sliding wins.
Where does N sit right now?
N's offset from the centre, computed by torque balance. It is zero when F = 0 and reaches w/2 exactly when F = Ftopple.

Topple or Slide

✦Learn this with the AI tutor

01

At a glance

A block stands on the floor while a horizontal push, applied at a height you choose, grows steadily from zero. Two thresholds compete, and the push height, the width and the friction decide which is reached first.

What you'll learn

  • How the forces and torques on the block balance as the push builds.
  • What sets the push needed to tip the block, and what sets the push needed to slide it.
  • How the push height a, the width w and the friction coefficient μ decide between the two.
The apparatus: a block of mass m, width w and height H on a floor with friction μ, pushed at height a.

What's on screen

  • Block with a blue dot at its centre of mass and a red dot at its front-bottom corner.
  • Force arrows: push F (pink), weight W (blue), friction f (amber) and normal force N (green).
  • Thresholds panel with Ftopple, Fslide and the Outcome.
See itLook at the block before the push starts. Watch for: the block, the pink F arrow at height a, the blue weight arrow W, and the green N arrow at the base.

03

The normal force moves forward as the push grows

While the block stays at rest, the forces and the torques on it balance. Vertically, the normal force N equals the weight W = mg. Horizontally, static friction f equals the push F and points back.

N need not act under the centre. Take torques about the middle of the base: friction and weight give none. The push turns the block forward with torque Fa, and N, acting a distance d ahead of the middle, turns it back with torque Nd. Setting them equal:

d = Fa / mg
d grows in proportion to F, and faster for a higher push a.

The base reaches only w/2 ahead of the middle, so d can grow up to w/2 and no further. At d = w/2, N acts at the front-bottom corner.

Forces on the block, not to scale. N acts a distance d ahead of the middle of the base.
See itPress Play with the opening settings and follow the green arrow. Watch for: the N arrow moving forward from under the centre as F grows, and the bar at the top left filling.
04

Toppling begins when N reaches the front-bottom corner

Once d = w/2, N cannot move further. N now acts at the front-bottom corner, so its torque about that corner is zero. The weight turns the block back about the corner with torque W·w/2, and the push turns it forward with torque Fa. The two balance at

Ftopple = mgw / 2a
The push at which Fa = W·w/2. Any larger push tips the block over the corner.

Ftopple falls as 1/a: halving the push height doubles it. It grows in proportion to the width w. At a = 0.90 m and w = 0.30 m it is 8.17 N, and a block 0.10 m wide needs only 2.73 N.

See itPress Play with the opening settings and wait for the end. Watch for: F reaching 8.2 N as N arrives at the front edge, then the block tipping over its front corner.
05

Sliding begins when friction reaches its limit

Static friction matches the push, f = F, but only up to a limit of μN. Since N = mg, the block starts to slide when

Fslide = μmg
Neither the push height a nor the width w appears here.

At the opening μ = 0.60 this is 29.43 N. Changing a moves only Ftopple, and changing μ moves only Fslide.

With μ = 0.10, Fslide is 4.91 N, below the 8.17 N that toppling needs at the opening settings. The push never gets high enough for N to reach the edge: it has moved only d = Fslide·a/mg = 0.09 m, which is 60 % of the way to w/2 = 0.15 m.

See itSet μ to 0.10 and press Play. Watch for: the block sliding at F = 4.9 N, the banner reading SLIDES, and the bar at the top left stopping at 60 %.
06

The smaller threshold decides what happens first

The push grows from zero, so it reaches the smaller threshold first. The block topples if Ftopple ≤ Fslide, and slides otherwise. Writing it out:

mgw / 2a ≤ μmg  ⟹  a ≥ w / 2μ
The mass m and g cancel.

So there is a critical push height a* = w/2μ. Push at or above it and the block topples. Push below it and the block slides. At w = 0.30 m and μ = 0.60, a* = 0.25 m. At exactly a*, the two thresholds are equal (29.43 N) and the sim reports TOPPLES.

Push height aFtoppleFslideOutcome
0.90 m8.17 N29.43 Ntopples
0.50 m14.71 N29.43 Ntopples
0.25 m29.43 N29.43 Ntopples (equal)
0.10 m73.57 N29.43 Nslides
See itDrop the push height to 0.10 m and press Play. Watch for: Ftopple at 73.57 N, well above Fslide at 29.43 N, and the block sliding with the Outcome reading SLIDES.
07

Width and friction move the critical height

  • Width w. A wider base raises Ftopple and raises a* in proportion. At a = 0.90 m, w = 0.80 m gives Ftopple = 21.80 N, still below Fslide, so the block still topples. At a = 0.50 m the same wide block slides, since a* = 0.67 m.
  • Friction μ. Only Fslide changes. A smoother floor raises a*, so more push heights end in a slide. A rougher floor lowers a*, so more end in a topple.
  • Mass and g. Both thresholds are proportional to m, so a* = w/2μ does not depend on the mass or on g.

The push height is limited to the block's height, a ≤ H = 1.0 m. A very smooth floor and a wide block put a* above that, and then the block slides at every height the sim allows.

See itSet w to 0.80 m and a to 0.50 m, then press Play. Watch for: Ftopple at 39.24 N, above Fslide at 29.43 N, so the wide block slides.
08

Where it matters

  • Vehicles in a turn. Treating the car as a rigid block, the sideways force acts like a push through the centre of mass at height h. With track width t, it rolls over before it skids when t/2h < μ. Tall, narrow vehicles and high loads lower t/2h.
  • Furniture. A cabinet 0.60 m deep on a floor with μ = 0.40 has a* = 0.75 m. Pushed higher than that it tips; pushed lower it slides.
  • Wide bases. Tripods, lamp stands and bar stools use a wide base to raise Ftopple = mgw/2a.
Go deeper

The sim stops raising the push at the first threshold, then plays a simplified tipping or sliding animation. It does not solve the motion afterwards. The tipping condition assumes the corner does not slip, which holds exactly when Ftopple ≤ Fslide.

09

Summary

In one line. A growing horizontal push reaches one of two thresholds first, and the sim shows how the push height, the width and the friction decide which.

Key points

  • N moves ahead of the centre by d = Fa/mg, and can go no further than w/2.
  • Ftopple = mgw/2a and Fslide = μmg. The smaller one is reached first.
  • The block topples when a ≥ w/2μ, and slides when a is below that.

Common mix-ups

  • "N acts under the centre of the block." It sits there only when F = 0. As the push grows, N moves forward by d = Fa/mg.
  • "A tall, narrow block always topples." Only if the push is at or above a* = w/2μ. Below that it slides.
  • "A heavier block is harder to topple, so it slides instead." Both thresholds scale with m, so a* does not change.

Things to try on your own

  • Set μ = 0.30 and w = 0.30 m. Work out a*, then check it in the sim.
  • At a = 0.40 m and μ = 0.60, find the narrowest width w that makes the block slide.
  • At the opening settings, find the μ below which the block slides.
